name: drm_dp_mst_process_up_req
prose: Static inline bool (drm_dp_mst_topology.c:4055-4098). It looks up the MST branch the request came from: for a broadcast header it uses the GUID of a DP_CONNECTION_STATUS_NOTIFY or DP_RESOURCE_STATUS_NOTIFY body (any other broadcast request type leaves no GUID and so no branch) via drm_dp_get_mst_branch_device_by_guid, and for a non-broadcast header it uses drm_dp_get_mst_branch_device with lct and rad. If no branch is found it returns false at once (no reference was taken). Otherwise, for DP_CONNECTION_STATUS_NOTIFY, if primary_mstb_probing_is_done is false it does nothing (CSN skipped), else it calls drm_dp_mst_handle_conn_stat, remembers whether that asks for more work, and sets the return value true. Resource-status notifications and other request types are not handled (the TODO). It then drops the branch reference with drm_dp_mst_topology_put_mstb, queues mgr->work on system_long_wq if the handler asked for work, and returns the hotplug flag, which is true only for a connection-status notification handled after probing finished; false for every other case, including a skipped CSN and unknown branch.
note: Checked against drm_dp_mst_topology.c:4055-4098. Reviewer claim (true for any resolved request, skipped CSN returns true too) is wrong: hotplug is initialised false (4062) and set true only in the else branch at 4089, which is reached only when probing is done. R:wrong

name: drm_atomic_helper_setup_commit
prose: Returns int. For every CRTC in the state it allocates a drm_crtc_commit (-ENOMEM on failure), initialises it, stores it in new_crtc_state->commit and calls stall_checks, whose error is returned (-EBUSY when nonblock is true and the CRTC's latest commit has not finished flip_done, or a negative errno from the interruptible wait for an older commit). If both the old and new CRTC states are inactive, or state->legacy_cursor_update is set, it completes the commit's flip_done and moves on. Otherwise, if new_crtc_state->event is NULL it allocates an event (-ENOMEM on failure) and stores it, then sets the event's completion to the commit's flip_done, takes references on the commit twice (one for the event, one for state->crtcs[i].commit) and sets abort_completion. For each connector, it returns -EBUSY when nonblock is true and the old connector state has a commit whose flip_done is not complete, then takes a commit from crtc_or_fake_commit (-ENOMEM when that returns NULL) and stores a referenced copy in new_conn_state->commit. Planes are handled the same way. At the end it returns the result of mode_config.helper_private->atomic_commit_setup(state) if that hook exists, otherwise 0. On any earlier error return, commits and references already stored in the state stay there for the caller's cleanup, and the hook is not called.
note: Checked against drm_atomic_helper.c:2508-2619 and stall_checks 2372-2420. Reviewer claims: (round 2) omits -EBUSY from a CRTC commit (right, stall_checks 2388-2394); (round 15) 'no event allocation occurs' is wrong (2553-2556 allocates an event), 'a hook error return means the hook was called' is right (2615-2616). R:mixed

name: drm_atomic_helper_check_modeset
prose: Returns int. For each CRTC in the state it WARNs if the CRTC mutex is not held; sets mode_changed when the mode differs; sets mode_changed and connectors_changed when enable differs; sets active_changed when active differs; returns -EINVAL if new_crtc_state->enable disagrees with whether the connector_mask is non-empty; and sets no_vblank true or false according to drm_dev_has_vblank. It then calls handle_conflicting_encoders (returning its error), and for each connector calls update_connector_routing (returning its error), marks the old CRTC's connectors_changed when the link status or max_requested_bpc changed, and calls the connector helper's atomic_check hook if present (returning its error). For each CRTC whose new state needs a modeset (drm_atomic_crtc_needs_modeset, i.e. mode, active or connectors changed) it calls drm_atomic_add_affected_connectors, drm_atomic_add_affected_planes and drm_atomic_check_valid_clones, returning the first error. It then calls atomic_check on connectors not yet checked, calls drm_atomic_add_encoder_bridges for the old and new best encoder of every connector in the state, and returns the result of mode_valid(state) if nonzero, else the result of mode_fixup(state). The state may be partially updated on an error return.
note: Checked against drm_atomic_helper.c:647-827. Reviewer claims: (a) precondition wrongly requires all connectors present, since the function adds affected connectors (right, 769-775); (b) 'adds connectors and planes only when CRTC enabled and connector_mask empty' is wrong: the condition is drm_atomic_crtc_needs_modeset at 760; and 'does not set active_changed/no_vblank' is wrong (692 and 703-706). R:mixed

name: drm_client_firmware_config
prose: Static bool (drm_client_modeset.c:619-803) that tries to reuse the firmware (BIOS) display configuration for a DRM client. It returns false at the start, before locking or modifying anything, when the driver does not use atomic modesetting, when min(connector_count, BITS_PER_LONG) is not positive (with a warning), or when the kcalloc of save_enabled fails. Otherwise it takes all modeset locks (retrying with backoff), saves a copy of enabled[], and counts connected tiled connectors. It then scans the first count connectors, repeating while it makes progress and some are not configured: a connector that is not enabled is marked configured; one forced off is set disabled but not marked configured; one without a best encoder (or whose state has no CRTC) goes to bail if its force is above DRM_FORCE_OFF, else it is disabled and marked configured; an enabled one counts as enabled, goes to bail if the same CRTC already appears in crtcs[], and otherwise gets its mode replaced by the cmdline, preferred, first, current-CRTC or (for incomplete tile groups) non-tiled mode, its CRTC stored in crtcs[i], and is marked configured with fallback cleared. Afterwards it calls drm_client_get_tile_offsets for each tiled connector, which fills the offsets array. If fewer connectors are enabled than detected and fewer than the CRTC count, or if no connector was configured, fallback stays or is set true. Both the fallback and bail paths restore enabled[] from the saved copy and make the result false (the modes and crtcs entries already changed are not restored). It then drops the locks, frees save_enabled and returns true only when neither bail nor fallback happened.
note: Checked against drm_client_modeset.c:619-803. Reviewer claims (from round 1): offsets are never filled (wrong, 769-776 call drm_client_get_tile_offsets), early false returns for non-atomic, count <= 0 and allocation failure (right, 638-646). R:mixed

name: drm_draw_color_from_xrgb8888
prose: Returns u32 by a switch on format with no side effects other than a possible one-time warning. For DRM_FORMAT_RGB888 and DRM_FORMAT_XRGB8888 it returns color unchanged. For DRM_FORMAT_RGB565, RGBA5551, XRGB1555, ARGB1555, ARGB8888, XBGR8888, ABGR8888, XRGB2101010, ARGB2101010 and ABGR2101010 it returns the result of the matching drm_pixel_xrgb8888_to_<format> conversion of color. For every other format it executes WARN_ONCE and returns 0. Any u32 values are accepted.
note: Checked against drm_draw.c:27-57. Reviewer claims about the RGBA5551 fourcc being wrong in the old prose (0x31414752 is not DRM_FORMAT_RGBA5551, which is 'R','A','1','5' = 0x35314152) are right; the prose now uses only symbolic format names. Contract left empty. R:right

name: add_3d_struct_modes
prose: Static int (drm_edid.c:4762-4794) that adds up to three 3D variants of the mode at VIC index vic_index. For each of bit 0, bit 6 and bit 8 of structure that is set, it calls drm_display_mode_from_vic_index; when that returns a mode it ORs in DRM_MODE_FLAG_3D_FRAME_PACKING (bit 0), DRM_MODE_FLAG_3D_TOP_AND_BOTTOM (bit 6) or DRM_MODE_FLAG_3D_SIDE_BY_SIDE_HALF (bit 8), passes it to drm_mode_probed_add (so the connector's probed list owns it) and counts it. The mode lookup returns NULL (adding nothing for that bit) when the connector has no VIC list, when vic_index is not below vics_len, when the VIC entry is 0, or when the mode allocation fails; a negative vic_index is not rejected by the check (it only tests vic_index >= vics_len) and would index before the array. It returns the number of modes added, from 0 to 3; the result is 0 when none of the three bits is set or all lookups failed, and a failure for one bit does not stop the other bits from adding modes.
note: Checked against drm_edid.c:4583-4593 and 4762-4794. Reviewer claims: partial success possible so result can be nonzero after an allocation failure (right, no early return), negative vic_index is not bounds-checked (right, 4589), formal-contract claim not applicable (contract left empty). R:right

name: drm_fb_helper_check_var
prose: Returns int and validates an fb_var_screeninfo request against the fbdev emulation framebuffer (drm_fb_helper.c:1205-1293). It returns -EINVAL immediately if in_dbg_master() is true. After that it sets var->pixclock to 0 when it was nonzero, so that change happens on every later path including the error returns. It returns -EINVAL if the framebuffer format is not DRM_FORMAT_C1, C2 or C4 and its plane-0 block width or block height is above 1; if var->bits_per_pixel exceeds the format's bpp or any of xres, yres, xres_virtual, yres_virtual exceeds the framebuffer width or height. It then calls __fill_var(var, info, fb), which rewrites the geometry and virtual sizes, and returns -EINVAL if yoffset or xoffset is greater than the virtual minus visible size, if var->grayscale > 0, or if var->nonstd is nonzero. Only after those checks, if all colour offset, length and msb_right fields are zero, it fills the pixel format fields with drm_fb_helper_fill_pixel_fmt. It then returns -EINVAL if the pixel format fields differ from info->var (drm_fb_pixel_format_equal), otherwise 0. Pixel-format filling therefore does not occur on the offset, grayscale or nonstd error returns.
note: Checked against drm_fb_helper.c:1205-1293. Reviewer claims: C1/C2/C4 exempt from the block-size -EINVAL (right, 1222-1233), omits -EINVAL for pixel format mismatch after normalisation (right, 1287-1289), pixel format filled only after the offset/grayscale/nonstd checks (right, 1258-1281). R:right

name: cdv_intel_lvds_init
prose: Void function (cdv_intel_lvds.c:477-667) that sets up the LVDS output on a Cedarview GPU. It returns having done nothing when dev_priv->lvds_enabled_in_vbt is false or lvds_is_present_in_vbt says no panel. It then allocates the encoder, connector and private data (returning, with partial frees through the error labels, when an allocation fails), creates the DDC i2c bus (GPIOC), initialises the LVDS connector and simple encoder, attaches the scaling-mode and backlight properties, and creates the backlight i2c bus on GPIOB with target address 0x2C, storing it in gma_encoder->i2c_bus and dev_priv->lvds_i2c_bus. Under dev->mode_config.mutex it reads EDID modes through psb_intel_ddc_get_modes and, if a preferred probed mode exists, stores a duplicate in mode_dev->panel_fixed_mode and jumps to out (even if the duplicate is NULL); otherwise it tries the VBT mode (duplicate marked preferred, jump to out if it succeeded), then, if the LVDS port is enabled and a CRTC exists for its pipe, the mode from the CRTC (marked preferred, jump to out if it succeeded). If panel_fixed_mode is still NULL it unlocks and unwinds everything (destroying the backlight bus, encoder, connector, DDC bus and freeing the private structures), so no LVDS output is registered. The PWM setup (BLC_PWM_CTL2 pipe select and PWM_ENABLE) is reached only when none of the three sources jumped to out yet panel_fixed_mode is non-NULL (for example already set before the call); when the mode comes from EDID, VBT or the CRTC the code jumps to out and does not program the PWM. It unlocks the mutex at out and returns void.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at cdv_intel_lvds.c:477). Reviewer claim (PWM not programmed when the mode is found via EDID or VBT; goto out before the PWM block) is right: gotos at 595, 606 and 624, PWM at 636-646. R:right

name: gma_find_best_pll
prose: Returns bool (gma_display.c:750-811). It picks clock.p2: if the crtc has an LVDS output and the LVDS port is enabled it takes limit->p2.p2_fast when the LVDS clock-B power bits show power-up and p2_slow otherwise; for other cases it takes p2_slow when target is below limit->p2.dot_limit and p2_fast otherwise. It zeroes *best_clock, then loops m1, m2 (bounded by m1 or any value when m1 is 0), n and p1 over the limit ranges, computes each candidate with clock_funcs->clock(refclk, &clock), skips candidates rejected by clock_funcs->pll_is_valid, and for accepted candidates whose abs(clock.dot - target) is strictly smaller than the best error so far (initially target) copies the candidate to *best_clock. It returns true if at least one accepted candidate improved on the initial error of target (so some candidate had error below target), and false otherwise, in which case *best_clock stays zeroed. It takes no locks.
note: slice cut the head: the function is gma_find_best_pll (gma_display.c:750), not cdv_intel_find_best_PLL (that name does not exist in this file). Old prose matched the code. R:n/a

name: hibmc_de_init
prose: Returns int (hibmc_drm_de.c:492-528). It initialises the primary plane with drm_universal_plane_init (logging and returning the error if that fails), adds the plane helper funcs, initialises the CRTC with drm_crtc_init_with_planes (error returned), sets the gamma size to 256 with drm_mode_crtc_set_gamma_size (error returned), adds the CRTC helper funcs and returns 0. On an error return it does not undo earlier steps (the plane or CRTC stays initialised); later steps are skipped.

name: ivch_mode_set
prose: Static void (dvo_ivch.c:399-440) that programs the IVCH panel-fit registers. It calls ivch_reset, which writes VR10 = 0 and then each backup register from priv->reg_backup, takes the last saved backup value as vr10 and sets vr01 to VR01_DITHER_ENABLE when its VR10_INTERFACE_DEPTH_MASK bits equal VR10_INTERFACE_2X18 or VR10_INTERFACE_1X18 (otherwise 0). vr40 starts as VR40_STALL_ENABLE | VR40_VERTICAL_INTERP_ENABLE | VR40_HORIZONTAL_INTERP_ENABLE. If mode->hdisplay or vdisplay differs from adjusted_mode->crtc_hdisplay or crtc_vdisplay, it also sets VR01_PANEL_FIT_ENABLE and VR40_CLOCK_GATING_ENABLE and writes the horizontal ratio to VR42 and the vertical ratio to VR41, each computed as ((mode size - 1) << 16) / (crtc size - 1) >> 2; a crtc_hdisplay or crtc_vdisplay of 1 makes that division by zero, so the caller must not pass one. VR41 and VR42 are written only in the size-mismatch case. In the other case it clears VR01_PANEL_FIT_ENABLE and VR40_CLOCK_GATING_ENABLE (they were not set). Finally it clears VR40_AUTO_RATIO_ENABLE and writes VR01 and VR40 on every call. It returns nothing.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at dvo_ivch.c:399). Reviewer claims: VR41/VR42 written only on size mismatch (right, 430-431), division by crtc size minus 1 when the value is 1 (right, 426-429), VR01 may also include VR01_PANEL_FIT_ENABLE (right, 424). R:right

name: g4x_hdmi_init
prose: Returns bool (g4x_hdmi.c:669-779). It returns false without allocating anything when assert_port_valid or assert_hdmi_port_valid fail. Otherwise it looks up the VBT child device data (a missing entry only logs), allocates a digital port (false if that fails) and a connector (on failure frees dig_port and returns false), initialises the encoder with drm_encoder_init as a TMDS encoder named by port (on failure frees connector and dig_port and returns false), fills in the encoder hooks according to PCH, Cherryview and Valleyview platform checks, sets type, power domain, port, pipe_mask, cloneable and hpd_pin, stores hdmi_reg in dig_port->hdmi.hdmi_reg, calls intel_infoframe_init, and calls intel_hdmi_init_connector; if that returns false it calls drm_encoder_cleanup, frees the connector and dig_port and returns false. Otherwise it returns true, leaving dig_port and the connector owned by the driver's encoder and connector lists.
note: slice cut the head: function is g4x_hdmi_init (head at g4x_hdmi.c:669; slice started at 762). The old prose treated the arguments as caller-allocated objects, which is not the case: the function allocates dig_port and the connector itself (690-696) and frees them on failure. R:n/a

name: ilk_wm_fbc
prose: Static u32 function (i9xx_wm.c:2420-2434). If cpp is 0 it executes WARN_ON and returns 0; otherwise, if horiz_pixels is 0 it executes WARN_ON and returns 0. Otherwise it returns DIV_ROUND_UP(pri_val * 64, horiz_pixels * cpp) + 2, computed in 32-bit unsigned arithmetic, so pri_val * 64, horiz_pixels * cpp and the DIV_ROUND_UP addend all wrap modulo 2^32 for large inputs; for inputs where nothing wraps the result is the ceiling of pri_val * 64 / (horiz_pixels * cpp) plus 2. It has no other effect beyond the warnings and takes no locks.
note: Checked against i9xx_wm.c:2420-2434. Reviewer claims: the contract omits the zero-argument WARN return path and the WARN side effect (right); an overflow input (pri_val=7, horiz_pixels=4294967285, cpp=1) falsifies the old contract (right, horiz_pixels*cpp wraps only for cpp>1 but the +d-1 addend in DIV_ROUND_UP wraps). Contract left empty because of the WARN side effect and u32 wrap-around. R:right

name: _i9xx_lut_10_ldw
prose: Static u32 function (intel_color.c:834-837) that returns drm_color_lut_extract(a, 10) & 0xff, i.e. the low 8 bits of the 10-bit value obtained from a 16-bit LUT sample. drm_color_lut_extract with 10 bits of precision returns DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST(a * 1023, 65535), which is (a * 1023 + 32767) / 65535 in unsigned arithmetic; for any u16 a the product fits in 32 bits. It has no other effects.
note: Checked against intel_color.c:834-837 and drm_color_mgmt.h:43-51. Reviewer claim (formal contract used /65536 and +32768 rather than rounding by 65535, e.g. a=65503 gives 254 not 255) is right; the replacement contract uses DIV_ROUND_CLOSEST's (x + 32767) / 65535. R:right

name: skl_commit_modeset_enables
prose: Static void (intel_display.c:6950-7106) that commits CRTC updates in a DDB-safe order. It computes entries[] and the pipe masks itself: for each CRTC whose new state is hw.active it records the old DDB entry and adds the pipe to update_pipes when no modeset is needed, otherwise adds it to modeset_pipes. It calls intel_pre_update_crtc (forward order) for the update pipes, calls intel_dbuf_mbus_pre_ddb_update, then loops until update_pipes is empty: in reverse pipe order it skips a pipe whose new DDB allocation overlaps another pipe's entry (retrying later; the loop has no other exit), otherwise records the entry, clears the pipe's bit, calls intel_update_crtc, and waits for the next vblank when that pipe's DDB changed and update_pipes or modeset_pipes still has bits. It then calls intel_dbuf_mbus_post_ddb_update, enables modeset pipes with intel_enable_crtc (first those that are neither joiner secondaries nor MST slaves or port-sync masters, then the remaining non-secondary ones, clearing each enabled pipe's joined pipe mask from modeset_pipes), calls intel_pre_update_crtc in forward order for the pipes that were modeset, and then calls intel_update_crtc in reverse order for them, with drm_WARN_ON on any DDB overlap. Finally it warns if modeset_pipes or update_pipes is not empty. It returns void.
note: Checked against intel_display.c:6950-7106. Reviewer claims: precondition wrongly requires the caller to precompute masks (right, 6959-6972); intel_pre_update_crtc for the modeset pipes runs forward, only intel_update_crtc is reverse (right, 7075-7101). R:right

name: intel_dp_detect
prose: Static int connector detect callback (intel_dp.c:5924-6063) whose return value is a connector_status_* value, or -EDEADLK. It warns if connection_mutex is not held. It returns connector_status_disconnected at once when the display device is not enabled, and returns the connector's existing status (connector->base.status) at once when intel_display_driver_check_access fails; neither of these paths touches PPS VDD. Otherwise it flushes pending connector commits, turns PPS VDD on, and determines a status: edp_detect for eDP, intel_dp_detect_dpcd when the digital port is connected, else disconnected; a non-disconnected status is turned into disconnected if intel_dp_mst_verify_dpcd_state fails. When the status is disconnected it resets the test and DSC/panel-replay sink state, calls intel_dp_mst_disconnect and intel_dp_tunnel_disconnect and jumps to out_unset_edid. Otherwise it initialises the source OUI and runs intel_dp_tunnel_detect: -EDEADLK is stored as the status and the function jumps straight to out_vdd_off (no EDID unsetting, no probe or subconnector update); a result of 1 bumps the epoch counter. It then reads PSR (non-eDP), DSC and SDP caps, resets the link params if requested, calls intel_dp_mst_configure, and if the port is in MST mode sets the status to disconnected and goes to out_unset_edid, with the MST and tunnel state left untouched and the EDID not unset because is_mst is true. In SST mode it checks the link state (non-eDP), clears the AUX NACK and defer counters, calls intel_dp_set_edid and sets the status to connected for eDP or when a detect EDID exists; if no EDID was read the status stays at the value determined earlier (it is not recomputed from the EDID read), then it checks the device service IRQ. At out_unset_edid it unsets the EDID when the status is not connected and not MST, turns the DPCD probe flag off and updates the subconnector property for non-eDP. At out_vdd_off it turns PPS VDD off and returns the status.
note: Checked against intel_dp.c:5924-6063. Reviewer claims: early returns skip VDD off and display-enabled is checked inside the function (right, 5942-5946); MST disconnected path skips EDID unset and MST/tunnel disconnect (right, 6013-6020 with 6049); status is not recomputed from the EDID read, it keeps the earlier value when no EDID (right, 6042-6044). R:right

name: intel_dp_aux_xfer
prose: Static int (intel_dp_aux.c:236-453) that performs one AUX transaction. It takes the digital port lock; for a non-eDP port that is not connected it returns -ENXIO after releasing only that lock. Otherwise it takes an AUX power-domain reference, takes the PPS lock for eDP or on VLV/CHV, turns VDD on (remembering whether this call did it), and sets the CPU latency QoS request to 0. It waits up to three times for the channel not to be busy; if still busy it returns -EBUSY after cleanup. It returns -E2BIG after cleanup (checked after the busy wait) when send_bytes or recv_size exceeds 20. It then tries each AUX clock divider, up to five attempts each, writing the send data and control, waiting for completion, clearing done/error status, retrying on timeout (continue) or receive error (after a sleep), and going to done on success; if no attempt completed it returns -EBUSY. At done it returns -EIO on a receive error, -ETIMEDOUT on a timeout, and -EBUSY when the reported message size is 0 or above 20. Otherwise it clamps the reply size to recv_size, reads the reply words into recv and returns that byte count, which is 0 when recv_size is 0. After the busy check, every return path restores the QoS request, turns VDD off only if this call turned it on, releases the PPS lock if taken, releases the power reference asynchronously, and unlocks the digital port.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at intel_dp_aux.c:236). Reviewer claim (success can return 0 when recv_size is 0, not 1..recv_size) is right: recv_bytes is clamped to recv_size at 431-432. The old prose also said it always releases a VDD reference it took; VDD is turned off only when intel_pps_vdd_on_unlocked reported it had enabled it (442). R:right

name: intel_dp_init_lttpr_phys
prose: Static int (intel_dp_link_training.c:147-195). It returns 0 if intel_dp_read_lttpr_common_caps fails, and 0 if drm_dp_lttpr_count of the common caps is 0 (no LTTPR). If the link is active it never changes the mode: for a negative count (an invalid caps value) or when transparent mode is already enabled it resets the repeater count byte and returns 0, otherwise it returns the positive count. If the link is inactive it calls drm_dp_lttpr_init(aux, count); when that returns nonzero (which includes every negative count, since it returns -ENODEV for them, as well as AUX write failures) it sets the transparent mode and resets the repeater count byte and returns 0; when it succeeds the count is positive, it sets non-transparent mode and returns the count. The function therefore returns 0 or a positive repeater count and never a negative value.
note: Checked against intel_dp_link_training.c:147-195 and drm_dp_helper.c:2919-2933, 2979-3008. Reviewer claims: out_reset_lttpr_count also resets the count byte on active links for transparent mode or negative count (right, 170-172, 191-194); a negative return is impossible when inactive because drm_dp_lttpr_init rejects negative counts (right, drm_dp_helper.c:2995-2996). R:right

name: bxt_ddi_pll_enable
prose: Static void (intel_dpll_mgr.c:2040-2146), returns nothing and reports no failure. It derives the port from pll->info->id (1:1 mapping) and the PHY and channel with bxt_port_to_phy_channel. It sets PORT_PLL_REF_SEL (non-SSC reference); on Geminilake it sets PORT_PLL_POWER_ENABLE and waits up to 200 us for PORT_PLL_POWER_STATE, logging drm_err if that wait fails. It clears the 10-bit clock enable, and read-modify-writes the P1/P2 fields (EBB0), M2 integer (PLL0), N (PLL1), M2 fraction (PLL2) and its enable (PLL3), the coefficient fields (PLL6), target count (PLL8), lock threshold (PLL9) and DCO amplitude fields (PLL10) from hw_state, then triggers recalibration through EBB4 and writes hw_state->ebb4. It then sets PORT_PLL_ENABLE, posts the read, and waits up to 200 us for PORT_PLL_LOCK, logging drm_err if it does not lock. Only after that, on Geminilake it ORs DCC_DELAY_RANGE_2 into the TX DW5 group register, and finally it writes the lane stagger fields into the PCS DW12 group register. A timeout is only logged; execution continues.
note: slice cut the head (function begins at intel_dpll_mgr.c:2040). Reviewer claim (the PLL enable and lock wait happen before the DCC and PCS DW12 writes, not after) is right: enable at 2122-2129, DCC at 2131-2135, PCS DW12 at 2141-2145. R:right

name: intel_fb_is_rc_ccs_cc_modifier
prose: Returns true when the modifier's entry in the intel_modifiers table has the INTEL_PLANE_CAP_CCS_RC_CC capability. That is the case for I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_MTL_RC_CCS_CC, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_DG2_RC_CCS_CC and I915_FORMAT_MOD_Y_TILED_GEN12_RC_CCS_CC. For every other known modifier it returns false. For a modifier that is not in the table, lookup_modifier executes WARN_ON and falls back to intel_modifiers[0] (the 4-tiled LNL CCS entry, whose caps are only INTEL_PLANE_CAP_TILING_4), so the result is false and a warning is emitted. It takes no locks and has no other effects.
note: Checked against intel_fb.c:248-358, 374-382 and 489-493. Reviewer claims about the old hex constants (round 1 and 15) are right that the old sets were wrong; the true set is the three modifiers named above, and (round 2) the unknown-modifier WARN_ON is a side effect that the old prose denied. The formal contract is dropped (hex values not verified). R:right

name: intel_fb_is_mc_ccs_modifier
prose: Returns true when the modifier's entry in the intel_modifiers table has the INTEL_PLANE_CAP_CCS_MC capability: I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_MTL_MC_CCS, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_DG2_MC_CCS and I915_FORMAT_MOD_Y_TILED_GEN12_MC_CCS. It returns false for every other known modifier. For a modifier not in the table, lookup_modifier executes WARN_ON and falls back to intel_modifiers[0] (the 4-tiled LNL CCS entry, whose caps are only INTEL_PLANE_CAP_TILING_4), so the result is false and a warning is emitted. It takes no locks and has no other effects.
note: Checked against intel_fb.c:248-358, 374-382 and 502-506. Reviewer claims about the old hex sets (rounds 1 and 15) and about the unlisted WARN_ON side effect (round 2) are right. R:right

name: intel_fb_is_tile4_modifier
prose: Returns true when the descriptor returned by lookup_modifier(modifier) has INTEL_PLANE_CAP_TILING_4 in its plane_caps. In the table that is I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_LNL_CCS, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_BMG_CCS, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_MTL_MC_CCS, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_MTL_RC_CCS, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_MTL_RC_CCS_CC, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_DG2_MC_CCS, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_DG2_RC_CCS_CC, I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED_DG2_RC_CCS and I915_FORMAT_MOD_4_TILED; every other known modifier gives false. For a modifier that is not in the table lookup_modifier does not return NULL: it executes WARN_ON and falls back to intel_modifiers[0], the 4-tiled LNL CCS entry, which has INTEL_PLANE_CAP_TILING_4, so the result is true together with a warning. It takes no locks.
note: Checked against intel_fb.c:248-358, 374-382 and 533-537. Reviewer claims: more than the low-byte 8..15 modifiers carry TILING_4 (right), the DG2 4-tiled modifiers carry it (right), and lookup_modifier can return NULL for unknown modifiers (wrong: line 378-379 falls back to intel_modifiers[0], so NULL is never returned). R:mixed

name: do_gmbus_xfer
prose: Static int (intel_gmbus.c:659-788) that performs an I2C transfer over GMBUS. It first disables GMBUS clock gating (display workaround) on Geminilake, Broxton, SPT or CNP platforms. It writes GMBUS0 and loops over the messages (an index read/write pair counts as two): each message is sent with gmbus_index_xfer, gmbus_xfer_read or gmbus_xfer_write, followed by a hardware-ready wait if that returned 0. A -ETIMEDOUT from a transfer or wait goes to the timeout path: GMBUS0 is cleared and the function returns -EAGAIN (to let the i2c core fall back to bit banging), not -ETIMEDOUT. Any other nonzero result goes to clear_err: it waits for idle, sets the result to -ENXIO, or -ETIMEDOUT if the idle wait failed, toggles the software clear-interrupt bit, clears GMBUS1 and GMBUS0 and, if the result is -ENXIO, the failing message is the first one and this is the first try, retries from the start once; otherwise it returns that result. When all messages succeed it writes a STOP cycle, waits for idle and returns -ETIMEDOUT if that wait fails, or the number of messages transferred (i, equal to num) otherwise; GMBUS0 is cleared on this path too. All paths re-enable clock gating before returning.
note: Checked against intel_gmbus.c:659-788. Reviewer claims: -ETIMEDOUT if the idle wait after STOP fails, so the bus is not always left idle (right, 709-714); round 15 claim that wait timeouts during a transfer return -ETIMEDOUT rather than -EAGAIN is wrong (693-694 goto timeout, 778 sets -EAGAIN). R:mixed

name: hdcp2_disable_encryption
prose: Static int (intel_hdcp.c:1957-1993). It warns (drm_WARN_ON) if LINK_ENCRYPTION_STATUS is not set in HDCP2_STATUS but does not stop, clears CTL_LINK_ENCRYPTION_REQ in HDCP2_CTL, and waits up to HDCP_ENCRYPT_STATUS_CHANGE_TIMEOUT_MS for LINK_ENCRYPTION_STATUS to clear (a -ETIMEDOUT result is only logged). If hdcp->shim->toggle_signalling is non-NULL it calls it with enable false and overwrites ret with its result: on failure it logs and returns that error, and on success ret becomes 0, so a wait timeout is hidden and the function returns 0. If toggle_signalling is NULL it returns the wait result (0 or -ETIMEDOUT or another wait error).
note: Checked against intel_hdcp.c:1957-1993. Reviewer claims (a successful toggle_signalling overwrites the wait result with 0, so the timeout is masked) are right (1982 assigns ret, 1992 returns it). The old prose both stated and contradicted this. R:right

name: intel_hdcp2_check_link
prose: Static int (intel_hdcp.c:2152-2236). It takes hdcp->mutex and then dig_port->hdcp.mutex itself and releases both at out before returning. It returns -EINVAL if hdcp->value is not DRM_MODE_CONTENT_PROTECTION_ENABLED or hdcp2_encrypted is false. If the hardware no longer reports HDCP2 encryption in use it logs, returns -ENXIO after _intel_hdcp2_disable and setting the value to DESIRED. It then calls shim->check_2_2_link: for HDCP_LINK_PROTECTED it sets the value to ENABLED unless the current value is UNDESIRED, and returns the status value it got (HDCP_LINK_PROTECTED); for HDCP_TOPOLOGY_CHANGE, if the current value is UNDESIRED it returns at once with that status unchanged, otherwise it re-authenticates the repeater topology and on success sets ENABLED and returns 0; on a failed topology authentication, or for any other status, it calls _intel_hdcp2_disable, sets the value to DESIRED and returns the disable result (0 on success, the error otherwise).
note: Checked against intel_hdcp.c:2152-2236. Reviewer claims: the old prose wrongly said the mutexes are held by the caller (right, 2161-2162), and it omitted the topology-change-with-UNDESIRED return and the protected-while-UNDESIRED case (right, 2187-2197). R:right

name: intel_hdcp_gsc_initiate_locality_check
prose: Static int (intel_hdcp_gsc_message.c:243-289). It returns -EINVAL if dev, data or lc_init_data is NULL, and -ENODEV (with an error log) if to_intel_display(dev) returns NULL. It takes display->hdcp.gsc_context (not checked), fills a wired_cmd_init_locality_check_in with API version, command id, success status, buffer length and the port type, physical port and transcoder from data, and sends it with intel_hdcp_gsc_msg_send; a negative result is returned unchanged. It returns -EIO if the reply header status is not FW_HDCP_STATUS_SUCCESS. Otherwise it sets lc_init_data->msg_id to HDCP_2_2_LC_INIT, copies HDCP_2_2_RN_LEN bytes of r_n from the reply into lc_init_data->r_n and returns 0. On every failure return lc_init_data is unmodified. It allocates nothing and takes no locks itself.
note: slice cut the head: the function is intel_hdcp_gsc_initiate_locality_check (head at intel_hdcp_gsc_message.c:243), not intel_hdcp_gsc_init_locality_check. Old prose matched the code. R:n/a

name: intel_pps_vdd_on_unlocked
prose: Returns bool (intel_pps.c:745-801). It records need_to_disable as the inverse of intel_dp->pps.want_panel_vdd at entry. If the port is not eDP it returns false immediately without changing anything. Otherwise it asserts (lockdep) that display->pps.mutex is held, cancels the delayed panel_vdd_work, sets want_panel_vdd to true, and if edp_have_panel_vdd reports VDD already on it returns need_to_disable without further action. Otherwise it warns if a vdd_wakeref is already held, takes the AUX power domain reference into pps.vdd_wakeref, waits for the panel power cycle when the panel has no power, sets EDP_FORCE_VDD in PP_CONTROL (with a posting read), and, if the panel still has no power, sleeps for panel_power_up_delay milliseconds. It returns need_to_disable, so for an eDP the return value is true exactly when want_panel_vdd was false on entry (the caller then owes a matching VDD off), whether or not VDD was already on in hardware.
note: Checked against intel_pps.c:745-801. Reviewer claims: the return bool is inverted / false when VDD already on (wrong: need_to_disable is returned at 762 and 800 and is !want_panel_vdd on entry); the early return for VDD-already-on skips the wakeref (correct, but the old prose already said the wakeref is taken only when VDD was not on); no eDP check exists (wrong: line 753 returns false for non-eDP). R:wrong

name: intel_psr_disable_locked
prose: Static void (intel_psr.c:2189-2257); the caller must hold intel_dp->psr.lock (lockdep assert). It returns at once if intel_dp->psr.enabled is false. Otherwise it calls intel_psr_exit (which also clears psr.active) and intel_psr_wait_exit_locked. On display version 11 and above it clears the pipe's LATENCY_REPORTING_REMOVED bit in GEN8_CHICKEN_DCPR_1. If sel_update_enabled it clears the DMASC clock-gating-disable bit only on the matching platforms: for display version 14.00 steps A0 to B0 without Panel Replay, in MTL_CLKGATE_DIS_TRANS; otherwise on Alderlake-P, in CLKGATE_DIS_MISC. For eDP it updates the SNPS PHY PSR power state to off, and for Panel Replay on eDP it disables ALPM. For PSR (not Panel Replay) it writes 0 to DP_PSR_EN_CFG on the sink and, with selective update, 0 to DP_RECEIVER_ALPM_CONFIG. For display version 20, or 30.00 steps A0 to B0, without Panel Replay it unblocks package C states. Finally it sets psr.enabled, panel_replay_enabled, sel_update_enabled, psr2_sel_fetch_enabled, su_region_et_enabled and psr2_sel_fetch_cff_enabled to false and active_non_psr_pipes and pkg_c_latency_used to 0; other psr fields (pipe, transcoder and so on) are not cleared by this function.
note: Checked against intel_psr.c:2189-2257. Reviewer claims: not all psr flags are cleared (right: only the fields listed at 2249-2256 are reset; intel_psr_exit also clears psr.active), the DMASC clear is platform and step conditional (right, 2216-2226). R:right

name: skl_plane_ctl_format
prose: Static u32 function (skl_universal_plane.c:945-1005) that maps a DRM fourcc to the PLANE_CTL format bits by a switch. Returned values: PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_INDEXED (C8), PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_RGB_565 (RGB565), PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_XRGB_8888 with PLANE_CTL_ORDER_RGBX added for XBGR8888 and ABGR8888 and without it for XRGB8888 and ARGB8888, the same pattern for the 2101010 and 16161616F families, PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_XYUV (XYUV8888), PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_YUV422 combined with the YUYV, YVYU, UYVY or VYUY order bits, PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_NV12, P010, P012, P016, Y210, Y212, Y216, and Y410, Y412, Y416 for XVYU2101010, XVYU12_16161616 and XVYU16161616. Any other format executes MISSING_CASE (a warning) and returns 0. Because PLANE_CTL_FORMAT_YUV422 and PLANE_CTL_YUV422_ORDER_YUYV are both defined as field value 0, DRM_FORMAT_YUYV also returns 0, so a zero result does not imply an unsupported format. It has no other effects.
note: Checked against skl_universal_plane.c:945-1005 and skl_universal_plane_regs.h:50, 75. Reviewer claims about wrong fourcc constants in the old contract (rounds 1 to 15) are right; additionally the old claim that every listed format maps to a nonzero value is wrong for YUYV. Contract dropped. R:right

name: skl_compute_plane_wm
prose: Static void (skl_watermark.c:1798-1934) that computes one watermark level into *result. It returns after writing only result->min_ddb_alloc = U16_MAX (the level is rejected, other fields untouched) when latency is 0, or when use_minimal_wm0_only holds and level > 0, or when the computed lines value is greater than skl_wm_max_lines(display); the line-count rejection happens after lines has been set to 0 for levels without line watermarks and does not depend on level. Otherwise it computes method1 and method2, selects a result (Y-tiled: max of method2 and the Y-tile minimum; non-Y-tiled: method2 for very small plane sizes, else method2 when latency >= linetime (min of both on display version 9), else method1), rounds it up to blocks (plus one below display version 30; raised to at least one line's blocks when skl_wm_has_lines), and computes lines; on display version 9 it applies WA 1125/1126 adjustments using result_prev->blocks, and on version 11 and above computes min_ddb_alloc from lines or blocks. Then it writes result->blocks, result->lines (0 when the level has no lines), result->min_ddb_alloc = max(min_ddb_alloc, blocks) + 1, result->enable = true and result->auto_min_alloc_wm_enable, and, only for display version below 12 with a nonzero sagv block time, result->can_sagv = latency >= sagv.block_time_us; otherwise can_sagv is left unchanged.
note: Checked against skl_watermark.c:1798-1934. Reviewer claims: more rejection paths exist (right, the lines check at 1913-1916); 'line-count rejection also requires level > 0' (wrong: no level test at 1913); 'result->lines is not zeroed when skl_wm_has_lines is false' (wrong: 1910-1911 zero it). R:mixed

name: i915_gem_execbuffer2_ioctl
prose: Returns int (i915_gem_execbuffer.c:3553-3642). It returns -EINVAL if check_buffer_count(args->buffer_count) fails, the error from i915_gem_check_execbuffer if that is nonzero, -ENOMEM if the kvmalloc_array of count + 2 elements fails, and -EFAULT (after freeing the array) if copy_from_user of the exec object list fails. Otherwise it calls i915_gem_do_execbuffer and keeps its result in err. Whatever err is, if args->flags has __EXEC_HAS_RELOC it tries to copy the updated offsets back: it opens a user write window on the user exec list (skipping the copy if that fails) and, for each entry with the UPDATE bit set, canonicalises the offset and writes it to the user list with unsafe_put_user, leaving the loop at the first fault; copy-back failures are ignored. It then clears __I915_EXEC_UNKNOWN_FLAGS in args->flags, frees exec2_list with kvfree and returns err, the result of i915_gem_do_execbuffer.
note: slice cut the head: the function is i915_gem_execbuffer2_ioctl (head at i915_gem_execbuffer.c:3553; the slice began at 3599). Old prose (best-effort copy-back, list freed, original err returned) matches the code but omitted the early error returns. R:n/a

name: igt_mock_exhaust_device_supported_pages
prose: Static int selftest (huge_pages.c:422-495). It saves RUNTIME_INFO(i915)->page_sizes and restores it at out_device on every return after the loop starts. For each non-empty subset of the page_sizes table it builds the combination (always including SZ_4K), sets the runtime page sizes to it, and for single = 0 and 1 creates a fake huge-page object (the error from fake_huge_pages_object is returned, via out_device), returns -EINVAL if obj->base.size differs from the combination (object put first), returns the error of i915_vma_instance or i915_vma_pin (object put first), then calls igt_check_page_sizes and, without testing its result first, compares vma->page_sizes.sg with the combination and sets err to -EINVAL on a mismatch (this overwrites an error returned by igt_check_page_sizes). It unpins and puts the object and goes to out_device if err is nonzero. After all subsets it returns err, which is 0 if every check passed. The function therefore stops at the first failing iteration, but within one iteration the sg check runs even after igt_check_page_sizes failed, so the returned error is the igt_check_page_sizes error unless the sg check also fails.
note: Checked against huge_pages.c:422-495. Reviewer claims: omits the i915_vma_instance error return (right, 461-465), sg check still runs after igt_check_page_sizes fails and can overwrite its errno (right, 471-477). R:right

name: igt_ctx_exec
prose: Static int selftest (i915_gem_context.c:659-782). It returns 0 immediately if the device has no logical contexts. For every uabi engine that can store a dword and has a nonzero context_size it creates a mock file (an error from mock_file is returned at once with nothing to release), starts a live test (igt_live_test_begin; an error goes to out_file) and, until the timeout, repeatedly creates a kernel context, creates a test object when needed (create_test_object), fills one dword with gpu_fill, throttles with throttle(), then releases the context. Errors from kernel_context, create_test_object, gpu_fill or throttle jump to out_file. After the loop it reads the dwords back with cpu_check on each object (an error breaks out of that loop). At out_file it releases the throttled requests, replaces err with -EIO if igt_live_test_end fails (even if err was 0), drops the file, and returns err from the function if it is nonzero. The other engines are not tried after an error. If every engine passes (or is skipped) it drains freed objects and finally returns 0; the initial err value of -ENODEV is never returned, because the last statement is return 0.
note: Checked against i915_gem_context.c:659-782. Reviewer claims: omits cpu_check and igt_live_test_end error returns (right, 762-764 and 771-772); the claim that -ENODEV is returned when no engine qualifies (round 1 and 15) is wrong, since err starts as -ENODEV but only a nonzero err set inside the engine loop is returned and the function ends with return 0 (781). R:mixed
